# Disposition of Bayl?s Warband

*Pages PDF 11-15*

## **Disposition of Bayl’s Warband**
This list represents the warband at full strength as they make their migration to the Southlands. Given their single-minded obsession with their goal their disposition is usually pretty simple, a dense mass of troops with a mounted contingent acting as scouts and outriders. 

- 16 Chaos Knights roving about the main force as outriders, split into four groups of four. 

- Main force consisting of Bayl and Dónalegur, 60 Chaos Warriors of Nurgle and 20 Chosen Chaos Warriors of Nurgle (Ryðklumpur and Tannpína among them). 

## Uniform
Bayl’s warband wear no uniform, though shades of brown and green predominate as is common among followers of Nurgle. 

## Shield Design
Bayl prefers his warriors to bear shields decorated with the eight-pointed star of Chaos, though as they travel south the thrice-lobed rune of Nurgle is becoming more openly displayed. 

## Battlecry
So, strangely enough, his tactics for the time being are to evade capture, refuse open battle, and escape from anyone who picks up his trail. 

Bayl places a lot of faith in his Chaos Knights to act as outriders. These mounted troops circle the main force, and rove ahead. Should they encounter a threat they must quickly make an appraisal of its strength. Either it can be overcome without risk or not. Even if the threat consists of a Roadwarden patrol or other small unit the Knights will try and provide information to the main force so that the warband can either navigate a way around without drawing attention, or else bring their full force to bear so that they leave no survivors and take no casualties. 

If the Knights realise that their movements have been detected, they use signals to communicate to each other and the main force before making misleading manoeuvres to confuse any observers. For example, if the Knights were to ride into the sight of a road busy with travellers, they might signal to the main force following them to move in a different direction, then head off in a third direction themselves in a conspicuous manner. In this way they would hope to distract the attention of anyone who sees them away from the main force, with whom they would rendezvous with once they had thrown off any pursuit. 

The warband use no particular batttlecry, though common rousing calls include ‘For the Plaguefather’, ‘Neiglen preserve us’, and various promises that the bodies of their opponents will soon become a breeding ground for flies and maggots. 

## Tactics
When he fought alongside his fellows of the Sarl tribe Bayl and his warriors formed a determined and resilient core that would tie up opposing regiments whilst faster moving elements of the Sarl force manoeuvred around the flanks. The task Bayl and his warriors undertook was not to deal out death or adopt clever tactics, but to be a rock against which the enemy forces would shatter. 

But that was before he took it upon himself to journey south and find Skrolk. Now Bayl and his warriors must undergo a dangerous journey through hostile nations, and no matter how tough and resourceful they are as warriors, they will not withstand organised opposition. Bayl may be able to overrun the militias of a Kislevite village, or even defeat the guards of an Ostland town, but every time one of his warriors falls in battle brings him one step closer to failure. He knows he must conserve his strength until his eventual meeting with Skrolk. 

## **Bayl of Many Eyes – Exalted Hero of Nurgle**
Despite his long devotion to Nurgle Bayl retains the proud bearing of the Sarl Norse, straight-backed and powerful. He is a cruel marauder but determined in his mission. He will forgo violence in order to find his way to Skrolk. 

Bayl wishes to win glory in the eyes of his foul patron and earn daemonhood. If he is presented with an opportunity to undertake a more promising mission, he may pursue it instead. This is a weakness a canny opponent may be able to exploit. Leading Bayl into conflict with followers of Tzeentch, or presenting him with a glorious challenge, may be enough to distract him, or even lead him into a trap. 

But such a trap must be carefully laid. Bayl has an odd mutation. Many wet eyes once opened in the flesh of his head, grew red and swollen, and then hatched into a swarm of flies. He still sees through them, granting him preternatural degrees of perception and insight.

## **Dónalegur – Exalted Hero of Nurgle**
Dónalegur is a faithful lieutenant to Bayl, having served as his right-hand man for several years in the bleak lands of the Troll Country. Stoic and unassuming, Dónalegur’s willingness to know his place and accept what fate throws at him has worked in his favour, for Nurgle is known to reward those who shoulder their fortunes with willingness, whether those fortunes are good or ill. The favour of Nurgle is clear on Dónalegur’s appearance, with several particularly grotesque mutations. 

Dónalegur may be complacent in his philosophy, but he is a fierce fighter and disciplined lieutenant, and Bayl relies on him to help organise and motivate the warband. Should the warband ever face determined opposition Dónalegur will find a place by his leader’s side, and fight to defend him until his last breath. 

A few years ago, Dónalegur lost a leg during a raid by Ungol horsemen. He bears the injury with his typical stoicism, and often makes pithy remarks about his missing limb.

## **Ryðklumpur – Chosen**
Ryðklumpur is growing frustrated. Not so long ago he fought at the vanguard of the raiding parties of the Sarl Norse, and whilst he was modest in his ambitions (most followers of Nurgle regard ambition as a somewhat unseemly character trait) he still felt the call to glory. He hoped to see more battles, hone his skills in war, and rise to the rank of champion, and perhaps even even attract the favour of the dark gods of Chaos. 

But he has had to leave that all behind him now, trudging league after league through the hinterlands of the Old World, with only the occasional raid on a farmstead to provide him with the opportunity for combat.

## **Tannpína – Chosen**
Tannpína has all the appearance of a Forsaken Warrior of Nurgle, being tough, heavily armoured, and hideously mutated. However, his mutations were not gifted by the dark gods, or even developed as a unnatural consequence of the hideous mutations common amongst those born to the tribes of the Norse. He was bred and altered within the depths of Hell Pit and raised for the purpose of sowing confusion and division amongst the enemies of Clan Moulder. 

Bayl believes that his mission to Skrolk’s library was bestowed in visions granted to him by Nurgle. The reality is that he has been set on his path by agents of Clan Moulder who hope that the warband will discover the existence of the Southlands Lair of Clan Pestilens. They surmise the lure of forbidden knowledge the Skaven possess should be irresistible to Bayl, and war between the followers of Nurgle and the Skaven Plague Monks will surely follow. Tannpína is their inside agent, making sure that Bayl sticks to his quest, and that when the Skaven are eventually discovered hostility is guaranteed.
